episode_title: Cultivating a Culture of Continuous Improvement with Mike Smart of Egress Solutions

real_qa.q: How should B2B SaaS companies balance adoption capabilities and onboarding with continuous product feature development?
real_qa.r: Mike Smart recommends that mid-market B2B SaaS companies should stop overemphasizing building new features and instead focus on making existing capabilities easier to adopt. He states that adoption is 90% of retention, and it is far more expensive to acquire a new customer than to retain and expand with existing customers through improved onboarding and adoption capabilities.
real_qa.requete: B2B SaaS adoption vs new product features

real_qa.q: What is the impact of buyers conducting 70% of purchase research before engaging with sales in B2B software sales?
real_qa.r: According to Gartner and other research, buyers are about 70% complete with their purchase decision before a salesperson walks in the door. This means salespeople cannot come in with basic information but must understand how to communicate with buyers where they are in their research journey, putting a high burden on go-to-market strategy and product marketing to build business cases and ROI justification.
real_qa.requete: 70% buyer research before sales contact B2B

real_qa.q: Why is cross-functional collaboration between sales, product, engineering, and product marketing essential from the ideation stage in B2B product development?
real_qa.r: Mike Smart emphasizes that sales, marketing, and engineering teams must sit at the table during the ideation stage of product development to think through the full customer lifecycle. If product marketing and go-to-market considerations are tacked on at the end, critical customer adoption, pricing, and messaging elements are missed, undermining the sales process and customer success.
real_qa.requete: cross-functional product development sales marketing engineering

real_qa.q: How does the iPhone and Apple's customer experience philosophy apply to B2B software product design and customer relationships?
real_qa.r: The iPhone set a standard for seamless unboxing and total package experience that B2B customers now expect at every touchpoint—finance, account services, customer support, and UX. If a company delivers an excellent product but makes it difficult to work with them operationally, the beautiful product is essentially shipped in a garbage bag, destroying the customer relationship and decision justification.
real_qa.requete: Apple iPhone B2B customer experience unboxing

real_qa.q: What does Atomic Habits principles mean for organizational change management in B2B companies?
real_qa.r: Mike Smart applies the Atomic Habits concept by recommending small, committed, repeatable changes rather than organization-wide disruption. Small changes are more sustainable and effective than big changes; they allow teams to feel progress, see results, and build momentum without strain, ultimately creating more successful organizational transformation.
real_qa.requete: Atomic Habits organizational change small incremental

real_qa.q: Why is iterative feedback between product management and sales teams critical when new products underperform in B2B markets?
real_qa.r: When a new product has sold only two units after seven months, product managers must loop back to sales teams to understand what buyers are saying and how the two successful sales were made. This feedback enables product managers to rethink messaging, features, and positioning based on real market signals rather than assumptions.
real_qa.requete: product management sales feedback loop underperforming B2B

guest.bio_context: Mike Smart founded Egress Solutions in 2009 and has spent 15 years working with mid-market B2B software and SaaS companies, biotech firms, enterprise software, health device companies, and fintech organizations. He specializes in helping these companies accelerate growth and market success through product management, focusing on software-centric and software-enabled revenue businesses.
